label: Fit to 4:3
tip: fit = letterbox/pillarbox, crop = fill 4:3, stretch = ignore aspect

label: Export fields
tip: interlaced: normal woven 576-line frame (both fields). 'field 1/2 only': only that field is rendered and every line is doubled -> a progressive, non-interlaced file (no combing, no interlace flags, ~2x faster). The GUI export also follows the 'Field 1/2 only' view selector

label: Field sampling
tip: temporal: field 2 is taken 1/50 s after field 1 (real interlace, combing on motion). frame: both fields come from one source frame (like film on PAL)

label: Interlace (anti-twitter) filter
tip: Vertical low-pass before the frame is split into fields

label: Bypass VHS (encoder -> TV only)
tip: Shows pure PAL encode/decode artefacts (cross-colour, dot crawl)

label: Tape speed
tip: LP/EP: narrower bandwidth, more noise

label: RF section sample rate
tip: 2x = 35.5 MHz (accurate FM sidebands, slower). 1x = 17.7 MHz: ~25% faster render, tiny differences

label: Head/preamp resonance (MHz)
tip: Head Q network peak. Service manuals tune VHS heads to ~4.9-5.0 MHz

label: Head/preamp resonance gain (dB)
tip: Boosts the upper FM sidebands (4.8 MHz white edges) and their noise

label: Tape/head noise (RF)
tip: White noise added to the RF signal, relative to carrier amplitude 1.0

label: Tape wear (signal loss)
tip: Overall RF level reduction -> more FM noise / sparkles

label: Colour-under record level (dB re FM)
tip: Burst amplitude of the 627 kHz colour-under relative to the unit FM carrier. Real decks record chroma ~20 dB under the luma FM (2-5 mV vs 25-70 mV at the record amp)

label: Chroma delay (ns)
tip: VHS chroma lags luma

label: Player colour lock (APC) speed
tip: Phase-lock of the colour up-converter to the burst: low = slow PLL, hue wobble from jitter survives

label: Colour-under phase sequence
tip: PAL VHS: head A unchanged, head B delayed 90 degrees each line in colour-under (JVC VTG82063). Legacy reproduces the old common rotation for comparison.

label: Head-switch model
tip: RF switch: localized RF loss and FM phase mismatch. Legacy overlay: original painted white snow. Off disables head-switch disturbance and masking, not other tape errors.

label: Switch before vertical sync (H)
tip: Nominal PAL VHS 6.5 H before broad vertical sync. One H is 64 us. Larger switches earlier/higher. Existing field timing remains a whole-line approximation.

label: Faulty servo vertical excursion (H)
tip: Explicit servo fault: vertical movement of the switch point. Zero for normal decks. Separate from horizontal line jitter and deterministic across seeks.

label: FM phase discontinuity (deg)
tip: Incoming-head carrier phase mismatch, opposite signs in the two fields. Produces a localized FM discriminator transient; not a hue control or random line shake.

label: RF interruption duration (us)
tip: Carrier-loss duration at head changeover. The demodulator produces the visible transient; this does not paint a white stripe.

label: RF recovery time constant (us)
tip: Exponential RF-envelope recovery after the interruption; larger values spread recovery along the scan line.

label: Head-switch shift variation (+- fraction)
tip: How much the shift size wobbles from frame to frame. 0 = the shift stays exactly at the set value (use together with 'Head-switch line jitter' = 0 for a perfectly steady shift)

label: Head-switch line jitter (us rms)
tip: Random left/right shake of every line in the head-switch zone

label: SWP black mask (field lines)
tip: Replace the last N active field lines with video black after playback; preserve sync and burst. Hides picture detail, not RF damage. Zero preserves full raster.

label: Head-switch snow strength
tip: Original-style waveform snow: a soft bright head, correlated grain and a fading tail, passed through the output and TV decoder. Zero disables it. Motion moves the streak, not the picture lines.

label: Snow follows head-switch line
tip: Anchors the top snow line to the first field line hit by the RF head switch (moved by 'Switch before vertical sync' and 'Faulty servo vertical excursion') instead of the fixed 'Snow gap to bottom'. Extra snow lines grow downward from it. An SWP black mask still hides snow underneath it.

label: Snow width (720-raster pixels)
tip: Nominal width/time scale in native 720-raster pixels. Length breathes per field as in the original effect, and filtering creates a soft tail beyond this nominal size. This is not a hard-edged pixel box.

label: Snow height (lines per field)
tip: One or two scan lines per field for the supplied reference. Each field has independent grain; the woven frame has twice as many interleaved rows.

label: Snow gap to bottom (woven-frame rows)
tip: Assumed interpretation of the supplied reference: number of full 576-line woven-frame rows below the snow band. The field grids differ by one row in parity. Independent of RF switch advance.

label: Snow base horizontal position
tip: Base horizontal start: 0 left, 1 right. Motion and position jitter are added relative to this point. Changes affect both preview and export.

label: Snow motion
tip: Move the narrow snow while playing or stepping frames. Motion changes snow position only, not picture-line timing or vertical position. Deterministic when seeking/exporting; paused frames stay still.

label: Snow drift (pixels per field)
tip: Horizontal travel each 1/50-second field in Drift modes. Negative moves left; zero stops steady drift. Bounces at the picture edges without clipping the snow width.

label: Snow jitter (pixels rms)
tip: Random horizontal jitter of the snow, different every field, plus a smaller independent jitter per snow line. Used by Random jumps and Drift + jitter (drift and jitter add up). This moves the snow patch, not the image scan lines. Zero disables jitter.

label: Snow sweep (pixels per field line)
tip: Horizontal offset for each additional snow line in the same field. Applies to every motion mode; zero aligns the lines vertically. Does not widen any individual streak.

label: Legacy head-switch snow streak
tip: Bright snow burst at the start (left) of the head-switch lines that fades out toward the right

label: Head-switch snow height (lines per field)
tip: How many scan lines of each field carry the snow burst (the two fields each have their own, so in the woven frame 1 = about 2 neighbouring rows). More lines fade out in strength

label: Head-switch snow drift (us/field, 0 = none)
tip: The snow burst moves horizontally from field to field: +7 us/field crosses the picture in ~7 fields (0.15 s) and wraps around. 0 = stays at the left edge

label: Head-switch snow base position (0 left .. 1 right)
Head-switch snow jitter (us rms)
tip: Random left/right jumps of the snow burst, different every field (jitter around the base position)

label: Head-switch snow sweep (us/line)
tip: Each following head-switch line starts the streak further to the right, so the snow flicks left to right

label: Dropout compensator (DOC)
tip: Player replaces dropouts with the previous line

label: Tracking knob (- noise at bottom, + at top)
tip: Manual tracking misadjustment. 0 = perfectly tracked. Negative: noise builds up from the bottom of the picture; positive: from the top. Larger |value| = more of the picture is covered, down to full snow

label: Snow streak density
tip: Long single-line white/black streaks in the noise of lost tracking. 0 = none

label: Snow streak length (us, typical)
tip: Median streak length in microseconds (64 us = full line); lengths vary around it

label: Sparse streaks over the whole frame (weak tape)
tip: Short white streaks on random lines anywhere in the picture, independent of the tracking band

label: Snow grain coarseness
tip: 0 = fine single-pixel noise, 1 = coarse horizontally stretched flecks

label: Tracking band: speeds up toward the bottom
tip: Same analog speed-up as for creases: slower at the top, faster near the bottom. 0 = constant speed

label: Tracking band: wobble (lines)
tip: Slow back-and-forth wobble of the tracking band position, in lines

label: Tracking band line smear/duplication
tip: Inside the tracking band the head reads the tape at a wandering speed: lines stretch/compress, shift sideways and repeat (long white/grey streaks, colour lost). Needs 'Tracking noise band' > 0

label: Travelling wrinkle (white band from the top)
tip: A crease band of random height enters at the top, runs down the picture and leaves at the bottom: its lines are duplicated / stretched and go solid white with ragged edges

label: White bands at once
tip: Exactly this many white bands are on screen at the same time (each with its own random height)

label: Gap between simultaneous bands (lines)
tip: 0 = random positions. Otherwise the bands follow each other at this distance (top to top)

label: Train length with several bands (frames)
tip: With 'White bands at once' > 1 the bands run as a train: each band that leaves at the bottom is replaced at the top, so exactly that many bands are on screen, for this many frames

label: White part height (lines, 0 = whole band)
tip: Size of the solid-white part, starting at the band's first (top) line. The duplicated (repeated) lines keep the size set by 'Band height min/max', so the white can be made smaller or bigger without changing the line duplication

label: Repeated (non-white) lines darkening
tip: The repeated lines of the band that are not in the white part are a copy of the line above the band. On a bright picture that copy also looks white; this fades it toward black so only the white part reads as white

label: Band enters at the top with full size
tip: On: the band is full height from the first picture line (no growing-in at the top, no duplicated white fields of the wrong size). Off: it slides in from above, growing line by line

label: Analog motion: speeds up toward the bottom
tip: Measured on real tape: a crease moves slowly at the top and 1.3-2x faster near the bottom. 0 = constant speed (digital look). The set speed is the average over the picture

label: Analog motion: wobble (lines)
tip: Slow sideways-in-time speed wobble of each band (tape tension), a few lines

label: Band grows in over (frames)
tip: A crease does not appear at full height: it starts thin (about a third) and thickens over these frames

label: Soft edges (top fuzzy, bottom crisp)
tip: 0 = hard line edges. The top edge of a real band fades in gradually, the bottom edge ends sharply

label: Satellite bands (thin companions)
tip: Thin secondary creases that travel together with the main band (about 0-2 per band at 1.0)

label: White flicker (field to field)
tip: The white part flickers: its brightness is dimmed by up to this fraction. The flicker is smooth in time (a few frames) with only a little field-to-field randomness

label: Band shrinks toward the bottom
tip: Bands lose height as they move down the picture. Each band gets its own random rate (0.4x-1.4x of this setting); a band that becomes smaller than about one line disappears, which can happen anywhere in the picture - above 1.0 many bands vanish before the bottom. 0 = constant height

label: Colour loss under the stretched lines (chance)
tip: Chance that a band also loses its colour over the whole stretched (repeated) area, not just in the white part

label: Band style
tip: white: solid white repeated lines. grey fade: grey lines that fade to black toward the bottom of the band with vertical streaks and no colour (head lifted off the tape, as on a blank blue tape)

label: Grey fade: top brightness
tip: Brightness of the top of a grey-fade band; it fades to black toward the bottom of the band

label: Band horizontal tear (0 = clean line repeat)
tip: 0 = the line above the band is repeated unchanged over the band height. Higher adds a random horizontal stretch/offset per line

label: Colour lock glitch (phase / saturation)
tip: Occasional episodes where the colour-under phase is lost: the whole picture turns green/purple with bands of wrong hue, then a saturated cast. 0 = off

label: Colour banding (slow line-group hue/saturation drift)
tip: Soft horizontal bands of slightly different hue and saturation, a few to tens of lines tall, drifting slowly (colour-under phase/gain instability, visible on flat colour such as a blank blue tape)

label: Colour glitch: one episode every (frames)
tip: Average spacing of colour-lock glitch episodes (one random episode inside every such period)

label: Colour glitch: episode length (frames)
tip: How many frames one colour-lock glitch episode lasts (it ramps in and out)

label: Wrinkle severity
tip: Creased tape: the head reads a local patch at a wrong, wandering speed (lines stretched/compressed, repeated or skipped, FM carrier shifted -> brightness stripes, chroma lost) plus head-lift dropouts

label: Wrinkle bands (usual wrinkle)
tip: Number of usual (stretch/skip) wrinkle bands in the picture at the same time

label: Gap between wrinkle bands (lines, 0 = spread evenly)
Vertical stretch (line repeat factor)
tip: 2.5 = each source line is shown ~2.5 times in the middle of the wrinkle (then lines are skipped to catch up)

label: Read-speed error (+- %)
tip: Tape speed error past the head. +10 % raises the FM carrier 10 % = ~+0.43 V brightness shift

label: Output level
tip: The TV AGC normalises this, but scope shows the level

label: Colour decoder
tip: PAL-D = delay-line decoder, PAL-S = simple (hue errors show)

label: Horizontal lock (AFC)
tip: 1.0 = ideal time-base corrector (wobble hidden); low = jitter visible
